F1.name: Adding/subtracting denominators as well as numerators

F2.name: Changing a denominator without scaling the numerator by the same factor
F2.example: Rewriting 1/3 as 1/6 rather than 2/6. Equivalent fractions must preserve the value.

F3.name: Changing the requested operation or reversing subtraction
F3.example: For 5/6 − 1/3, correctly rewrite 1/3 as 2/6, then add 5 + 2. Subtract 5 − 2, giving 3/6. Preserve the original order when subtracting.

F4.name: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction incorrectly
F4.example: 2 1/3 → 3/3 rather than 7/3. Two wholes are six thirds, then add the remaining third.

F5.name: Regrouping a whole as one fractional part
F5.example: When subtracting 3/4 from 2 1/4, rewrite 2 1/4 as 1 2/4. One whole supplies four quarters: the correct regrouping is 1 5/4.

F6.name: Simplifying only one part, or using different changes to numerator and denominator

F7.name: Cancelling across addition/subtraction as if multiplying
F7.example: Cross-cancelling the two 2s in 2/3 + 1/2 to obtain 1/3 + 1. Use equivalent fractions over a common denominator; the sum is 7/6.

F8.name: Converting an improper fraction back to a mixed number with the wrong fractional unit
F8.example: 7/3 → 2 1/7. The remainder is still one third: 2 1/3.
